decision.note: Records carry their company; the contract must therefore only return stored records.

content.statement: Users are accounts of a company, records are contacts and deals, and sharing is a table of shares.
content.why: A record belongs to the company stored on it, and a user to the company of their account. This trusts the record: ReadContract therefore requires returned records to be the stored ones.
substitutions: sharedWith := (r: CrmRecord, t: TenantId) => shares.value.contains(Share(r.id, t))

decision.note: Users only see records through searches.

content.statement: Records are shown only as query results, and a query returns only records the user may see.
content.why: Users find records by searching, so what a user sees is what their queries return. abs: a user is shown a record when some query of theirs returns it.

sources.spec: run => forall((u: User.T, q: Query.T) => run(u, q).forall(r => visible(u, r)))
sources.abs: run => (u, r) => exists((q: Query.T) => run(u, q).contains(r))

decision.note: Covers search by id, kind and everything, as the idea lists.

content.statement: A search returns stored records only, each of the user's company or shared with it.
content.why: Accounts, stated for one call. A returned record must be one of the stored records, so an implementation cannot relabel another company's record as the user's.

sources.post: (user, query, result) => result.forall(r => store.value.contains(r) && (r.tenant == user.tenant || shares.value.contains(Share(r.id, user.tenant))))

examples: expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), Everything) ⇒ ::(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), List())  given store.bind(List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Kind.Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Kind.Contact, "Globex contact"))), shares.bind(Nil)  — Ann lists everything she can see: Acme's deal

expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), ById(2)) ⇒ List()  given store.bind(List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Kind.Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Kind.Contact, "Globex contact"))), shares.bind(Nil)  — Globex's contact is not shared with Acme

reject (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), ById(2)) ⇒ ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())  given store.bind(List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Kind.Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Kind.Contact, "Globex contact"))), shares.bind(Nil)  — another company's record is never returned

reject (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), Everything) ⇒ ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("acme"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())  given store.bind(List(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Kind.Deal, "Acme deal"), CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Kind.Contact, "Globex contact"))), shares.bind(Nil)  — a record relabelled as Acme's is not a stored record

expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), OfKind(Contact)) ⇒ ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())  given store.bind(List(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Kind.Contact, "Globex contact"))), shares.bind(List(Share(2, TenantId("acme"))))  — Globex shared its contact with Acme, so Ann finds it by kind

decision.note: Isolation between companies is the promise of a shared CRM.

content.statement: A user sees a record only if it belongs to their company or was shared with their company.
content.why: Isolation between companies is what the idea says must hold. Companies, users, records and sharing are left open.

sources.spec: shows => forall((u: User.T, r: Record.T) => shows(u, r) ==> visible(u, r))
